title: Blinded by acid at 3. Topped her blind school at 18. October 19, 2026.
excerpt: From the astrophysicist born this day in 1910 who proved what crushes a dying star, to a Padma Bhushan honoree who built a cancer hospital in Hyderabad while practicing in New York, October 19's five stories are about what gets built across distance - across decades, across oceans, across impossible odds.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about something built across a gap that should have made it impossible - a theory proven decades before anyone could confirm it, a hospital built in Hyderabad by someone practicing in New York, an engineering career that turned into leading an AI giant 36 years later, an EV market that kept climbing month after month instead of spiking once, and a blind school topper who studied by audiobook after losing her sight at three.

October 19, 1910: a boy was born in Lahore who would spend his career proving what crushes a dying star

Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, born in Lahore, spent nearly six decades at the University of Chicago and won the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for showing that a white dwarf star's mass can't exceed about 1.44 times the Sun's - the Chandrasekhar limit.

He joined an American tech giant as an engineer in 1990. In 2026, TIME named him one of the 100 most influential people in AI

Arvind Krishna, chairman and CEO of IBM since 2020, was named to TIME's 2026 TIME100 AI list - one of roughly ten Indians and people of Indian origin honoured, after joining IBM's research division in 1990 following an IIT Kanpur degree.

He spent decades treating cancer in New York. India just gave him its third-highest civilian honour

Dr. Dattatreyudu Nori, a longtime Cornell Medical Center oncologist, received India's Padma Bhushan in 2026, having co-founded the 500-bed Basavatarakam Indo-American Cancer Hospital in Hyderabad while still practicing in the US.

India just crossed 3 lakh EV registrations for the fourth month running

India registered 3,33,571 electric vehicles in September 2026, per government Vahan data - the fourth consecutive month above 3 lakh, on pace to beat 2025's record 2.27 million annual total by a wide margin.

Blinded by acid at 3. Topped her blind school at 18

Kafi, attacked with acid during Holi 2011 in Hisar, Haryana, studied through audiobooks at Chandigarh's Institute for the Blind and topped the school's humanities stream in CBSE Class 12 with 95.6% when results were declared in May 2025.

Five stories, one pattern: a theory that took decades to be confirmed, a hospital built across an ocean from where its founder practiced, an engineering career that compounded into AI leadership over 36 years, a market trend that proved itself month after month rather than once, and a mind that kept learning after losing the sense most people learn by.
